steps.text: To make the rub: Stir salt, white sugar, brown sugar, black pepper, white pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, chili powder, paprika, and cumin together in a small bowl.
Rub spice mixture all over ribs; cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
To make the sauce: Stir apple juice, brown sugar, and barbeque sauce together until well combined. Set aside.

Unwrap ribs and arrange in a single layer onto the wire racks of the smoker. Place the racks into a smoker, fill the smoker pan with apple, grape, pear, or cherry chips, and heat the smoker to 270 degrees F (130 degrees C). Cook ribs for 1 hour.
Brush ribs with sauce and continue cooking, basting with sauce every 30 to 40 minutes, until pork is no longer pink and begins to shrink back from bones, 3 to 4 hours.
Brush sauce onto ribs one last time and remove them from the smoker. Wrap ribs tightly with aluminum foil and allow to rest until juices reabsorb into meat, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Smoked Pork Ribs
raw_recipe.description: This smoked ribs recipe cooks baby back pork ribs coated with a spicy rub, and basted with a sweet BBQ sauce until tender in a smoker.

video.description: Fall off the bone sweet smoked ribs will be a pleaser for your favorite meat eater! Moist ribs with flavorful apple juice, brown sugar, cumin and other lovely savory spices. Enjoy this with a side of coleslaw and potatoes for a filling meal!

review.reviewBody: Oh my, these are finger lickin' good! I may be a Northern girl, but I do know a good rib when I taste one. The key to a really good rib is in the rub and this rub is great! I actually made extra and put it in a small jar to have on hand. I did change one major thing though and that was the amount of salt - I cut way back on that; 1 & 1/2 tsp. for the full recipe. The rest of the recipe is a matter of taste. I used 1 Tbsp each of the black and white peppers, but really you could leave it alone. We have a smoker, but if you don't use whatever you have - gas or charcoal grill with a lid. If you do use a grill, wrap the ribs in foil and put a thin layer of BBQ sauce on the bottom of the foil before wrapping to prevent the ribs from sticking. Place them on the grill on low heat, cover, and let them cook for about two - three hours or until done. Unwrap them and finish directly on the grill basting the ribs in the remaining BBQ sauce. As far as the BBQ sauce is concerned again use what you have or like. I didn't have apple juice so I added a splash of apple cider vinegar, a splash of liquid smoke along with the brown sugar to some Bull's Eye BBQ sauce I had (I doubled the amount the recipe called for). These were absolutely fabulous, fall off the bone good - perfect with coleslaw and cornbread.

Great recipe! I do not have a smoker so I added a small amount of liquid smoke to the dry rub. I also added 1/4 cup of apple juice to the dry rub and let the ribs marinate for 6 hours. I grilled the ribs on my gas grill and brush them with the BBQ/apple juice/brown sugar mixture frequently. They came out so tender and the taste was perfect. I served the ribs with a side of grilled zucchini/yellow squash and couscous. Enjoy!!! :-)

I modified the dry rub and cooking process a little bit and they turned out absolutely fantastic!! Decreased the salt slightly and used 1 extra tbsp of brown sugar and one tbsp less of white sugar. Then smoked on the Traeger @ 275 for 1 hour. spritzed with apple juice, let go another 45 minutes, basted with BBQ sauce and spritzed again and let go 15 more minutes to set. Then double-wrapped in foil (meat side down) with a little rub on the bottom with pads of butter and a drizzle of honey and let them go another 1.5 hours. Everyone said they were the best ribs they have ever had.

Pretty perfect! That's what my husband and daughter said after eating the spare ribs that I made using your rub. I used all ingredients except the cumin and white pepper because I don't have those and I used only 1 tbsp of salt. I put the rub on and wrapped it in plastic wrap over night. I smoked the two racks for 3 hours on 225 in an electric smoker with hickory chips; then put apple juice on them with a basting brush; wrapped in aluminum foil and put back in the smoker for 2 hours; then put BBQ sauce thick on the racks and smoked for another 30 minutes. Will definitely have this as my go-to rub for ribs!

Amazing rub and ribs came out falling of the bone. Ensure you get ribs with lot of meat to ensure they are moist. Used Traeger grill. Avoided white sugar and added some pepper flakes to give a kick. Used jack Daniels honey smokehouse and kc master piece with little A1 smoky mesquite sauce with some pineapple teriyaki sauce . To keep them moist used frozen apple juice and little apple cider vinegar with spoon of left over rub mix.

On Saturday my Masterbuilt 30" smoker arrived. After doing the preheating (cleaning the unit) on Sunday, I gave this recipe a try. Not knowing what to expect, I asked my wife & her family to have something else ready for dinner that night. 

This recipe made me look like a hero. The ribs came out perfectly....even though I did not follow the recipe exactly (I did not marinate the ribs in plastic in the refrigerator as listed). I added apple chips every time I was basting (soaked only for 20 minutes) & left the top vent open fully. 

I would suggest that you check the meat after 4 hours...my smoker cooked it faster than expected. Most importantly, cover the ribs in foil...this really adds to the flavor. The best part of the recipe is the aroma that your house receives when brining in the ribs...

Thanks again!

Recipe makes enough rub for 2 racks of ribs. I cut the black and white pepper amounts in half to get a little less bite after finding the same amount in another recipe to be overpowering. Also tried only doing the glaze on one of the racks of ribs and found the non-glazed ones were actually a little more moist and tender. That said, they did both stay in a little longer than intended while prepping the other parts of the meal. If I do them again, I'll probably wrap them in foil with some of the glaze in the foil, halfway through cooking, to see if they get a little more tender while retaining more juices. They weren't overly dry or tough, but not quite what I was hoping for, on that front. Very good flavor, though. Will definitely experiment with it to see how I can get them more tender and juicy. As a side note, I didn't realize I ran out of cherry wood for the smoke, so I had to use hickory. Turned out to be a decent alternative, though apple or cherry would likely be best.

The appearance of the finished product looked spectacular. My mouth watered as I split the ribs into two bone sections. My first bite of the bark shocked me! I'm a salt driven eater, but this was over the top salty. My next attempt, I'll reduce the salt by half or perhaps double the total weight of the pork ribs. The meat was fall off the bone, moist and the fat rendered out. If it weren't so salty I would have ranked it higher.

Dadcooksagain!! 10 stars if I could! I am not even a big rib fan but these turned out phenomenal!! Followed exactly but did on our Traeger @ 270. Started at 1pm and pulling them off around 5:30pm. Fall off the bone tender and the flavor was….WOW! For the basting sauce - made as written; just used Famous Daves original BBQ sauce (blue bottle) - which, I didn’t think this was too sweet at all?! These were so, SO good that I’m already planning to make these either for the 4th or July or an upcoming family get together in July we have planned. I know these will be a hit with my family! Thank you for sharing this recipe! A keeper!

I decided to try this recipe. I do them on a gas grill, with a wood chip box. I also put a baking sheet under the grill grate and fill it with water in order to maintain moisture. I keep the grill at 270°. Following this recipe they've turned out absolutely incredible. You can slow cook on a gas grill. You've just got to know your grill and use wood chips for smoke, at the right time. I've made some spectacular racks of baby back ribs using this method! I highly recommend this recipe.

This is a really good rub, without being overly spicy. Per other reviewers' recommendations, I cut back on the amount of salt to about 1 1/2 tbs. I smoked the ribs with apple wood chips and basted during the last couple of hours with a mixture of apple juice and bbq sauce. The family loved them!
Even better as leftovers, but maybe only because I needed to smoke them a little longer than I did.
Great flavour and easy to follow.

This was my first time smoking anything at all, so I used this recipe since it seemed good and easy to follow. I followed the advice of those who said to reduce the salt and pepper amounts in the rub and threw in some more brown sugar. It was delicious! I don't think I heard a peep from the family while we were digging into these. Thank you very much for the recipe. I feel emboldened by this success and I'm excited for my next smoke! :)

Made this several times and every time it's a game winner. No complaints from the meat eaters! The only suggestion is all smokers are different. I lower the temp to 255 after the 1st hour at 270 and done 4.5 hrs later.
I found it very salty, next time I would try it with half the amount.
My go to ribs recipe
Little longer cook time lower heat
We added red pepper and hot spices. We like it hot and it was so delicious. Thank you for the recipe. Keep them coming Yummy for my families tummy. 😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋😋

Good but way too much pepper. I like hot, I like pepper, but it tasted like a lot of black pepper. I recommend cutting back on the portion of black and white pepper. I wouldn't hesitate adding more brown sugar.
